newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps - gasoline firmly in pole position.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps - gasoline firmly in pole position.

text.p: Gasoline swaps were the dominant player in the European oil swaps market on Thursday, gaining $2-3 a tonne.
Naphtha was $1 or so stronger, riding on gasoline's strength, while Brent crude CFDs were a few cents higher and fuel was flat.
U.S. data released earlier this week showed a draw in gasoline stocks combined which with tight prompt supplies in NWE and the Mediterranean combined to push swaps higher, traders said.

August gasolilne swaps were pegged around $207 with the September backwardation widening to $9 or so. Prompt material was very hard to find but better supplies from August 15 onwards will take some the fire out of current swaps levels, dealers said.
Naphtha was $1 or so higher, effectively on the back of gasoline's rise although supplies were also fairly tight. August was pegged at $192.00 with September backwardated by $3-4 or so.
Brent CFDs were a touch firmer with August 4-8 firming to +6 cents against September Brent compared with +3 cents with August 11-15 sy -3/4 cents from -4 cents.
August 18-22 was put at -8 cents from -10 cents and August 25-29 was pegged at -13 cents.
Dealers said activity was very slow with the market divided about the timing of resumed Iraqi exports.
Gas oil crack spreads steepened, but prices were broadly notional with little concrete trade occurring, traders said.
4Q and 1Q were seen around $4.55 with 2Q unchanged at $4.00.
